destinations.name: The Dead Sea - The Lowest Point on Earth
destinations.location: Dead Sea, Jordan Valley, Balqa / Madaba Governorates
destinations.description: The lowest point on Earth at 427m below sea level, offering healing mineral waters, natural mud baths, and historic heritage sites.

destinations.name: Ma'in Hot Springs (Hammamat Ma'in)
destinations.location: Madaba Governorate, 27 km southwest of Madaba, near the Dead Sea
destinations.description: A natural thermal oasis located 264m below sea level, featuring mineral-rich hot waterfalls heated up to 63°C by underground volcanic fissures.
destinations.bestTime: Autumn, Winter & Spring / Early Morning or Evening

destinations.name: Aqaba - The Coastal Gem of Jordan
destinations.location: Aqaba Governorate, Southern Jordan (4 hours drive from Amman)
destinations.description: Jordan's coastal city on the Red Sea, offering world-class diving, water sports, luxury resorts, and a rich historical heritage dating back to early Islamic and Mamluk eras.

destinations.name: Azraq Wetland Reserve
destinations.location: Azraq, Eastern Desert, Zarqa Governorate (115 km East of Amman)
destinations.description: A unique wetland oasis in the Eastern Desert, listed under the Ramsar Convention and IUCN Green List, serving as a vital sanctuary for migratory birds and the endemic Sarhani fish.

destinations.name: Pella (Tabaqat Fahl)
destinations.location: Northwestern Jordan, Eastern hills of the Jordan Valley (Ghor)
destinations.description: An ancient Decapolis city with over 6,000 years of history, featuring Classical theaters, ancient tombs, Byzantine churches, and an Umayyad mosque overlooking the Jordan Valley.

destinations.name: Wadi Hidan
destinations.description: A dramatic black-basalt canyon featuring natural pools, flowing water, waterfalls, and vegetation. You can experience hiking, swimming, and canyoning while moving through the narrow canyon.*You should expect to get wet

destinations.name: Ajloun
destinations.description: Ajloun is a green mountainous destination in northern Jordan, known for its forests, historical sites, and outdoor activities. Its main attractions include the historic Ajloun Castle, Ajloun Forest Reserve, Mar Elias, and several hiking and nature trails.Ajloun is particularly known for its green landscapes and wildflowers during spring.

destinations.name: As-Salt
destinations.description: As-Salt is a historic Jordanian city known for its distinctive yellow-limestone architecture, traditional streets and stairways, historic houses, cultural heritage, and traditions of hospitality.The city's historic core contains approximately 650 significant historic buildings and reflects architectural influences from the late Ottoman period, including European Art Nouveau and Neo-Colonial styles combined with local traditions.
destinations.bestTime: Morning to late afternoon / Autumn & Spring

destinations.name: Iraq Al-Amir
destinations.location: Wadi Al-Seer, southwest of Amman, Jordan
destinations.description: A historical and natural destination famous for its Hellenistic heritage, olive trees, springs, and ancient caves. Its most important archaeological landmark is Qasr Al-Abd (Qasr Al-Abed), one of the few surviving examples of pre-Roman architecture in Jordan. The area also offers cultural experiences through the Iraq Al-Amir Women's Cooperative, where visitors can learn about traditional handicrafts and local heritage.

destinations.name: Madaba
destinations.description: Madaba, known as the “City of Mosaics,” is one of Jordan’s most important cultural and religious tourism destinations. It is particularly famous for its Byzantine and Umayyad mosaics, especially the 6th-century Madaba Mosaic Map preserved in the Greek Orthodox Church of St. George. The city also offers archaeological sites, museums, traditional handicrafts, and access to nearby attractions such as Mount Nebo and Umm ar-Rasas.

destinations.name: Dana Biosphere Reserve
destinations.description: Dana Biosphere Reserve is the largest biosphere reserve in Jordan and was established in 1989. It was designated as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 1998. The reserve is characterized by dramatic mountains, deep valleys, sandstone formations, diverse ecosystems, and rich biodiversity. It contains three major biogeographical regions and is home to a wide variety of plants and wildlife. Some of its best-known trails include Wadi Dana, Wadi Ghweir, White Dome, Nawatef, and Rummana Mountain.

destinations.Description: Petra, the Rose City is one of the Seven Wonders of the World and an ancient Nabataean city dating back more than 2,000 years.It is an entire city carved into rose-red rock, resembling a fortress, built by the Nabataeans and serving as their capital.

destinations.Categories: History & Culture · Hidden Gems · Food & Local Experiences
destinations.Description: Karak Castle is one of the largest and most important castles in Jordan. The castle has been converted into an archaeological museum since 1980. The museum displays Muslim artifacts from the Ottoman period, and it has a section that covers the Neolithic, Bronze and Iron Ages.

destinations.Location: Near the Dead Sea, south of Amman
destinations.Description: The Mujib Biosphere Reserve is The lowest nature reserve in the world, located in a deep valley reaching 410 meters below sea level, and is characterized by great biodiversity due to the difference in elevations and water flow.

destinations.Categories: Nature · Adventure · Relaxation · Food & Local Experiences · Hidden Gems
destinations.Description: Wadi Rum – also known as the Valley of the Moon – is characterized by its desert landscapes, sands, mountains, and stunning sunsets. It also features historical sites and offers activities such as evening entertainment, telescope viewing, and hot air balloon rides.
A restored Roman theater dating back to the 2nd century AD, built on the slopes of three hills, with a capacity of approximately 6,000 people, it's still used for performances.

A 13 km nature reserve spanning the Ajloun Highlands, encompassing diverse forests of plants and animals, making it suitable for nature lovers visiting Jordan. Picnics and hiking, especially in spring
